newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia propels Helsinki to record close.
newsitem.headline: Nokia propels Helsinki to record close.

text.p: Shares ended broadly higher on Wednesday, with a Nokia-led rally driving the main indices to a record high close and advancing U.S. stocks pointing the way to further gains this week, brokers said.

The FOX portfolio index rose 1.43 percent to a life-high close of 1,230.79, topping its previous July 25 peak close by eight points. The all-share HEX added 1.77 percent to a record high 3,587.15 point close. Advancers beat decliners 67 to 25.
"This market feels like it will continue upward," one broker said, adding: "there's not much worry about the U.S. economic data due at the end of the week."
But volume was only moderate, at just over 500 million, and some brokers said the market could run out of steam before Nokia's first-half earnings report next Monday.
Nokia jumped in early trade after rising on Wall Street overnight. It ended up 18.50 markka at a life-high 466.00 close, after setting an all-time intraday high of 469.00.
Brokers said expectations of a good January-June report from Nokia were pumping up the share.
Metra rose sharply in fair demand fuelled by the strong dollar, brokers said. Metra B rose 10.00 markka to 188.00 and the less-traded Metra A added 10.00 to 189.00.
Forestries also rose with help from the strong dollar. UPM gained 0.40 markka to 132.90 and was the second most traded share after Nokia, accounting for eight percent of volume.
Metsa-Serla rose 1.80 markka to 47.50 and added a point to the FOX index's 17-point gains.
Outokumpu rose in fairly lively trade and ended up 0.80 markka at 103.80, despite volatility in zinc prices.
But Merita dragged the index, falling 0.50 markka to 22.80 in fair 22 million markka volume. Brokers said it eased in the absence of recent heavy buying pressure.
Amer built on its Tuesday gains, up 4.00 markka to 100.00.
